CHIEF COMPLAINT
Perioral dermatitis with residual rash.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a Fitzpatrick skin type IV individual presenting with ongoing perioral dermatitis and rosacea. She reports that symptoms have improved significantly on doxycycline twice daily for the first two weeks. One week ago, she reduced doxycycline to once daily based on pharmacist recommendation, after which improvement plateaued and rash did not continue to resolve. She denies current breastfeeding. She attempted monotherapy with doxycycline alone and did not use elidel cream due to concerns after reading about the medication. Physical examination reveals faint erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks and mild redness around and underneath the nostrils. Patient reports sun sensitivity and states she takes precautions with hat and protective clothing when outdoors.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies dryness or thinning of facial skin. Denies worsening symptoms. Reports good tolerance of sulfacetamide wash and metro cream.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis
Rosacea, including ocular rosacea

MEDICATIONS
Doxycycline 100 mg once daily (recently reduced from twice daily)
Sulfacetamide wash twice daily
Metro cream applied once daily after face wash

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is not currently breastfeeding. Reports sun sensitivity and uses protective measures including hat when outdoors.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV (does not burn, sun tans). Bilateral medial cheeks with a few faint erythematous papules. Mild erythema around and underneath nostrils. Rash not completely resolved.

RESULTS
Not applicable

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis and rosacea, including ocular rosacea.

1. Increase doxycycline back to 100 mg twice daily until rash resolves, then continue once daily for one additional week before discontinuing.
2. Add tacrolimus ointment 0.1% (calcineurin inhibitor) to affected areas twice daily until rash is gone, then discontinue. Counseled that transient tingly or needle-like sensation may occur 5-10 minutes after application lasting only seconds and is not an allergic reaction.
3. Continue sulfacetamide wash daily (patient prefers twice daily; discussed reducing to once daily if dryness develops, but will allow patient to continue twice daily as tolerated).
4. Continue metro cream daily.
5. Cancelled elidel cream from medication list. Discussed that concerns about malignancy apply to oral form in high doses long-term after transplantation, not topical as-needed use.
6. Cancelled clindamycin from medication list.
7. Recommended basic moisturizer such as Vanicream or petroleum jelly as needed. Provided samples.
8. Patient counseled regarding doxycycline side effects: potential gastrointestinal upset/heartburn and photosensitivity requiring sun protection.
9. Advised against use of steroids on face and against new or anti-aging products without discussion.
10. If rash worsens, patient to contact office or send MyChart message.
11. Once rash resolves, patient to hold off on restarting old products until follow-up visit.
12. If minor flare occurs, can trial tacrolimus alone for a few days; if insufficient, restart doxycycline as well.
13. For ocular involvement: gently wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as Vanicream; use Bruder mask as needed.
14. Follow-up appointment in approximately 4 weeks.
15. Patient has adequate refills of doxycycline and metro cream.
